Coordinate the following home page expansion across Big Brother and Stef. Apply logicVerification from the Big Brother checklist system before any implementation begins — restate the logic below in plain terms, confirm RESOLVED or UNRESOLVED, and only proceed once resolved.

1. Verify current home page structure first (Big Brother):
Confirm the home page is laid out as two columns — left and right — each a 3×10 grid with placeholders. 2. Button placement rule (Big Brother, ongoing — not just this batch):
Every time Pete says "add button," Big Brother adds the next button starting from the last reference point, filling in this order: left column, top-left start, left to right, then descending (i.e., fill row 1 left→right, then row 2 left→right, and so on, left column before right column). Big Brother must track the last-filled position so future "add button" requests continue from there without Pete having to specify placement each time.

Agents

Each gets its own placement per the rule above (left column, next open slots, left-to-right, descending).

4. Each button needs its own HTML page (Big Brother creates the button + link; Stef creates the page content):
For each of the three buttons, Big Brother creates the button on the home page grid, wired to open a corresponding standalone HTML page. Stef designs and builds each page as a "future content" placeholder that doubles as an art/graphics expression — not a generic "coming soon" page. Requirements for Stef:

Each page should read as Stef's own design suggestion / MCP experiment — genuine expression and variation between the three pages, not three copies of the same template with different labels. Vary layout, motif, visual language page to page, the way a graphic designer would show range across a set.
Stef should take the current Command Portal design system into account (the existing dark/amber/cyan palette, JetBrains Mono + Inter typography, card/border/radius conventions already established) so each placeholder feels native to the portal, not bolted on — but still has room to riff and propose ideas within that language.
Each page serves two purposes simultaneously: (a) a functional placeholder Pete can click into before real content exists, and (b) a genuine design sample/pitch for what that section could become once populated.
When Pete later tells Big Brother what to actually populate a given page with, that page gets rebuilt with real content at that time — Stef's placeholder is explicitly temporary/exploratory, not final.

5. Set up per-agent config-criteria and checklist-config, same pattern as Big Brother's system:
For each agent involved in this task (starting with Olivia, Big Brother, and Stef), set up the same two-file structure already established in big-brother-checklists/:

A config-criteria.json entry (or file, if agent-specific criteria differ meaningfully from Big Brother's) defining what "done correctly" means for that agent's role — e.g., Stef's criteria should include things like "design coherent with existing portal system," "genuine variation across placeholder set," "clearly marked as placeholder, not permanent," "responsive/no broken layout."
A checklist-config.json entry per agent tracking actual current state, lastVerified, status, and knownIssues — same schema discipline as the command-portal entry already created (don't invent ad hoc categories in checklist-config; new categories belong in config-criteria first).

6. Olivia's role — review, modify, validate, verify, confirm, report:
Once Big Brother and Stef report their work back to you, Olivia must:

Review the actual output against the requirements above.
Modify anything that doesn't meet spec (wrong grid position, pages that aren't genuinely varied, missing config files, etc.) by sending it back to the responsible agent — don't accept and pass through work that fails review.
Validate the grid structure claim in step 1 was actually true and the three buttons landed in the correct positions.
Verify each of the three HTML pages exists, loads, and meets both the placeholder and design-expression requirements.
Confirm the per-agent config-criteria/checklist-config files were created correctly and follow the established schema.
Report a single consolidated status back — RESOLVED (everything above confirmed correct) or UNRESOLVED (list exactly what's outstanding) — and hand that verified update to Pete for review before it goes back to Claude.
